verdict.rationale: Svelte's own tooling surfaces diagnostics: `sv check` reports errors and warnings such as unused CSS, accessibility hints and JS/TS compiler errors, and a community user praises the compiler's specific compile-time warnings (e.g. 'A11y: element should have an alt attribute'). Nothing documents how clear or actionable dev-server or build-time error output is, and one user wishes SvelteKit were at Next.js's level because fixing dev server errors is distracting. missing for 10: documentation of dev-server error overlays or messages, documentation of build-failure error output with fix guidance, independent corroboration that runtime and dev-server errors are actionable

support.subject: As a developer, I can get clear, actionable error messages from the dev server and build tool when something breaks

citations.quote: `sv check` finds errors and warnings in your project, such as: unused CSS, accessibility hints, JavaScript/TypeScript compiler errors
You can also check your code from the command line using npx sv check.
Praises Svelte 3's built-in compile-time accessibility warnings (e.g. 'A11y: element should have an alt attribute')
